findings.detail: The new docblock (lines 41-43) states the `*-latest` aliases "sit last in their own family as a permanent backstop". Neither list matches that. In `quality`, `gemini-pro-latest` is index 1 and the dated Pro id `gemini-2.5-pro` follows it at index 2. In `fast`, `gemini-flash-latest` is index 2 and the dated `gemini-3-flash-preview` follows it at index 3. Since `resolveModel()` returns the first non-retired candidate and the docblock's own premise is that a `-latest` alias "cannot be retired", every entry after the alias in the same family is unreachable except in the per-key/per-project NOT_FOUND case the file documents at lines 76-88. So either the ordering is wrong or the comment is — and the new test only pins presence (`.some((m) => m.endsWith('-latest'))`), not the position the comment claims, so appending a dated id after an alias would keep passing. This is the exact failure shape the PR is correcting: a comment asserting a property of the list that nothing checks.
findings.summary: Comment says the -latest aliases sit last in their family; in both tiers they don't

findings.detail: Lines 30-31 copy both ordered candidate lists into the ADR. `services/geminiService.ts:45` in this same diff declares that file "the ONLY place model ids live", and line 50 of this ADR is a consequence bullet about a document that claimed Pro while the code ran Flash. A hand-maintained second copy of the lists reintroduces precisely that drift: the next `MODEL_CANDIDATES` edit silently makes this ADR wrong, and nothing fails (there is no test in `tests/unit/` that reads any file under `docs/`, so the new pin in `geminiModels.test.ts` does not cover this). The lists are also the least durable part of the ADR — the tier *mapping* table below is the decision worth recording; the ids are an implementation detail with a documented expiry date.
findings.summary: ADR now enumerates both tier lists verbatim, duplicating the source of truth

findings.detail: `AQ\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}` is derived from a single sample ("the observed key is ~50 characters", giving ~47 chars after the dot — about 7 characters of margin). For a scanner, the failure mode that costs something is a false negative: a shorter `AQ.`-prefixed key variant would pass the sweep silently, which is the same class of hole this commit is closing. The prose-collision risk the floor guards against is small — `AQ.` followed by 20+ unbroken `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` characters does not occur in English text, and I confirmed the pattern currently matches nothing in the tree (tracked or untracked), so lowering the floor costs no false positives today. Not raised above info because the current floor does catch the credential this project actually uses, and the rationale is recorded on the line above.
findings.summary: AQ. pattern's 40-char floor is tuned to one observed key
